why: Item 1 holds for the verifier brief. Check 1 passes when the call returns {} without throwing, and it states "Any stderr warning the change prints is allowed." The file-path warning appears only as an advisory note, outside PASS/FAIL. Item 2 breaks in the builder brief. Step 2 tells the builder to do more than return {} on a parse error: "before returning `{}`, write one line to stderr ... that names `path` and includes the parse error's message". It bases this on "The issue's real complaint" and not on the acceptance line. Steps 3, 5 and 6 then build on this warning in the JSDoc, the README and the manual check. Item 1 calls logging a warning more than returning {}, so telling the builder to log one on parse errors counts as an action beyond returning {}, which item 2 forbids.
